decision_adr-initiative-timeline-dates ADR: Initiative timeline dates and Scheduled vs Backlog content/decisions/decision_adr-initiative-timeline-dates.md decision active team Operations decision_linear-ontology-adoption decision_deflate-ontology doc:content/decisions/decision_linear-ontology-adoption.md code:scripts/lib/frontmatter-schema.mjs code:scripts/lib/indexer.mjs code:apps/board/src/lib/types.ts ## Context

[`decision_linear-ontology-adoption`](decision_linear-ontology-adoption.md)
(2026-04-01) added `initiative` as the 6th artifact type and defined two optional
extension fields — `x_timeline_start` and `x_timeline_end` — while **forbidding**
`due_date` and `iteration` on initiatives. The timeline fields were specified but
never wired into the pipeline: `buildManifestEntries` promotes only `x_phase→phase`
and `x_author→author` (`scripts/lib/indexer.mjs:204–212`), so any `x_timeline_*`
value survives only inside `meta_json` and is invisible to `index/manifest.jsonl`
and the board `ManifestEntry` type.

Two facts as of 2026-07-01:

1. **0 of 39 initiatives** use `x_timeline_start`/`x_timeline_end` (`grep` over
   `content/initiatives/`). Initiative timing is inferred ad hoc from child-task
   `due_date`s — only ~6 active initiatives have any future-dated child task.
2. A management need has surfaced: view initiatives on a Linear-style **timeline**
   (horizontal date bars) with **expandable child tasks**. That requires a
   queryable initiative date *and* a rule for the majority of initiatives that
   carry no date yet.

The schema already accepts the fields, so `./hey validate` does not block them.
What is missing is (a) pipeline wiring and (b) an agreed semantics for dated vs
undated initiatives. This ADR settles both. It does not reverse the parent ADR;
it operationalizes the timeline fields the parent ADR reserved.

## Decision

**1. Promote `x_timeline_start`/`x_timeline_end` to first-class indexed fields.**
Extract both in `indexer.mjs` (mirroring the `x_phase→phase` line), normalized via
`normalizeDueDate` (strip time; accept `YYYY-MM-DD` or ISO 8601), and surface them
as `timeline_start` / `timeline_end` in the manifest, the SQLite `items` table, and
the board `ManifestEntry`/`Initiative` types. The frontmatter schema needs **no
change** — the fields are already in `TYPE_FIELDS.initiative`.

**2. Semantics — target date plus optional start.**
`x_timeline_end` is the initiative's **target / launch date** (the field members
mean when they say an initiative's "due date"). `x_timeline_start` is **optional**.
Rendering: both present → a **bar**; target only → a **milestone point**.
Initiatives continue to carry **no `due_date`** (unchanged from the parent ADR) —
the timeline signal is `x_timeline_end`.

**3. Scheduled vs Backlog is decided by the explicit target.**
An initiative **with** `x_timeline_end` is **Scheduled** and renders on the
timeline. An initiative **without** it is **Backlog** and renders in a separate
section. For Backlog initiatives a date **derived** from child-task `due_date`s MAY
be shown as a greyed, explicitly-labeled hint — **never** as a timeline bar.
Writing a target date is the explicit act that promotes an initiative onto the
roadmap.

## Scheduled vs Backlog — definitions

| Term | Rule | Timeline rendering |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Scheduled** | has explicit `x_timeline_end` | bar (if `x_timeline_start` also set) or milestone point |
| **Backlog** | no explicit `x_timeline_end` | listed in a separate section; derived date (max child `due_date`) shown only as a greyed hint |

Rationale: there is no `backlog` status value (statuses are `active` / `done` /
`archived`), so **date-presence is the classification signal**. Deriving a bar for
every initiative from child-task dues would place stale bars in the past (e.g. a
lone April-dated task) and manufacture false precision; keeping derivation as a
hint-only affordance keeps "backlog = not yet committed" honest and makes the
unscheduled gap visible to owners.

## Consequences

- The board can render an initiative timeline, and `./hey db query` can
  filter/sort initiatives by `timeline_end`.
- **Backfill is owner-driven, not auto-written.** The initiative scaffold template
  gains the two fields (new initiatives are prompted from day one); a helper lists
  each active initiative with its derived suggestion; owners set their own targets.
  alice seeds alice-owned initiatives; other owners receive an inbox heads-up with
  the derived suggestion. No mass auto-write — that would fabricate commitments on
  another owner's behalf.
- **Coordination:** the indexer / SQLite / validator touch points sit in charlie's
  area (owner of the linear-ontology ADR and the `scripts/lib` pipeline).
  Implementation is coordinated with charlie.
- The validator gains a **soft** check: warn when both fields are present and
  `x_timeline_start > x_timeline_end`. Neither field is required.
- Member-facing timeline surfaces lead with the initiative `title`, per
  [`decision_adr-display-task-titles-not-ids`](decision_adr-display-task-titles-not-ids.md).
- **Out of scope (deliberately deferred):** in-UI date editing / write-back
  (fast-follow), and goal linkage + goal swimlanes (a separate ADR — goals will be
  modeled without a new artifact type, honoring `decision_deflate-ontology`).

## Alternatives Considered

- **Add a fresh `target_date` (or re-allow `due_date`) on initiatives** — rejected.
  It duplicates the already-reserved `x_timeline_*` fields and reintroduces
  `due_date`, which the parent ADR forbids for a reason: initiatives are strategy,
  not iteration-bound work items.
- **Derive the timeline for every initiative from child-task dues (no explicit
  field)** — rejected. Produces stale/misleading bars and gives owners no way to
  commit an intentional, visible target.
- **Introduce a `backlog` status value** — rejected. Needs new vocab plus manual
  classification and duplicates the signal that target-presence already carries.
- **Add a `goal`/`project` mid-tier now for grouping** — out of scope, and
  constrained by `decision_deflate-ontology` (avoid confusable type proliferation).
  Goal grouping is a later, lighter-weight change.

## Code Changes Required (for the follow-on build)

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/lib/indexer.mjs` (~line 204) | Add `timeline_start: normalizeDueDate(fm.x_timeline_start)` and `timeline_end: normalizeDueDate(fm.x_timeline_end)` |
| `apps/board/src/lib/types.ts` | Add `timeline_start` / `timeline_end: string \| null` to `ManifestEntry` |
| `scripts/lib/catalog-db.mjs` | Add two nullable columns to the `items` table |
| `scripts/lib/validate.mjs` | Soft warning when `x_timeline_start > x_timeline_end` |
| `scripts/lib/scaffold.mjs` | Add `x_timeline_start` / `x_timeline_end` to the initiative template |
| `scripts/lib/frontmatter-schema.mjs` | **No change** — fields already permitted |

documents.title: ADR: KB-wide change contracts with qmd as the primary deps-gate recall channel
documents.text:
decision_adr-kb-wide-change-contracts ADR: KB-wide change contracts with qmd as the primary deps-gate recall channel content/decisions/decision_adr-kb-wide-change-contracts.md decision Team active team Engineering Infrastructure Operations decision_adr-qmd-local-retrieval-backend doc:content/decisions/decision_adr-qmd-local-retrieval-backend.md doc:content/notes/2026/06/note_qmd-benchmark-2026-06-02.md doc:docs/TEMPLATES.md ## Context

The dependency knowledge base started as nine hand-authored notes under
`content/notes/dependencies/`, each carrying an `x_change_contract`
(triggers → obligations → verification). `./hey deps check` — a MUST-run gate
before change-intent work (`AGENTS.md` Dependency Checks) — matched only those
nine records, out of ~2,560 content artifacts.

Two structural problems surfaced (investigation 2026-08-10):

1. **Coverage cannot scale by hand.** Obligation-bearing knowledge already
   lives across the KB — playbooks with checklists, decisions with
   consequences, notes with "Required Follow-Ups" — but none of it entered the
   gate unless someone duplicated it into a dedicated dependency note.
2. **The authoring burden was mostly retrieval plumbing.** The validator
   required hand-enumerated `triggers.terms[]` (including Korean phrase
   variants) whose only purpose was making *lexical* matching fire. qmd's
   hybrid retrieval makes that unnecessary: MRR 0.714 vs lexical 0.521 on the
   149-query benchmark, and 0.520 vs 0.239 on sentence-style queries
   (`note_qmd-benchmark-2026-06-02`).

## Decision

1. **The contract pool is KB-wide.** Any non-workspace content artifact
   (note, decision, playbook, task) may opt in with the `ChangeImpact` tag +
   `x_change_contract` frontmatter and joins the `deps check` pool.
   `notes/dependencies/` remains a valid home for standalone dependency
   knowledge, but is no longer the only one. Terminal-status artifacts
   (`done`/`archived`/`cancelled`) drop out of the pool: their obligations are
   historical record, not binding checks on new work.
2. **qmd is the primary recall channel for the deps gate — promoted, still
   per-machine optional.** `deps check` runs semantic recall whenever the qmd
   index is available (refreshing it in place when stale). Without qmd it
   degrades to structured + lexical matching, but **loudly**: a stderr notice
   states that recall is degraded and how to enable qmd. The per-developer
   opt-in stance of
   [`decision_adr-qmd-local-retrieval-backend`](decision_adr-qmd-local-retrieval-backend.md)
   is retained, not amended.
3. **`triggers.terms[]` and `intents[]` become optional precision boosters.**
   The validator requires at least one trigger signal of *any* kind
   (repo/path/area/entity/intent/term) plus obligations, but no longer
   requires hand-authored terms. Recall comes from qmd plus full title/body
   lexical matching, which the matcher already performs.
4. **The deterministic obligation layer stays.** Obligations with severity
   (`required`/`recommended`/`watch`), verification checks, Non-Trigger
   Records, and the aggregation consumed by `hey mission compile` remain
   structured and code-evaluated. `mission compile` intentionally stays
   structured + lexical: mission packs are written artifacts and must not vary
   with per-machine qmd state.
5. **Contracts are distilled, not hand-authored, going forward.** The `/clean`
   hygiene checklist gains a distillation step: scan recently updated
   artifacts for obligation-bearing sections lacking a contract and propose
   `x_change_contract` frontmatter as a reviewable diff. The agent extracts;
   the human approves; code checks.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Status quo (nine notes + mandatory terms).** Rejected: coverage stuck at
   nine records and every new dependency taxed authors with retrieval plumbing
   that qmd does better.
2. **Pure retrieval — retire contracts, let the agent read qmd top-k and infer
   obligations.** Rejected: turns a MUST-run gate probabilistic, loses
   severity semantics, Non-Trigger Records, and the deterministic obligation
   aggregation `mission compile` depends on. If code can answer, code answers.
3. **Make qmd required for the gate.** Deferred: it would amend the accepted
   per-developer opt-in ADR for a ~318 MB install win that the loud fallback
   notice largely delivers. Revisit if degraded-recall notices show real
   misses on non-qmd machines.

## Consequences

### Positive

- Any existing decision/playbook can start binding obligations with a
  frontmatter block — no parallel note to author or keep in sync.
- New contracts need no `terms[]` enumeration; the qmd channel and body-text
  matching carry recall in both languages.
- Non-qmd machines keep working, and now *know* their recall is degraded
  instead of silently missing semantic matches.

### Negative

- Pool membership is broader, so `deps check` precision depends more on the
  acceptance thresholds in `scripts/lib/deps.mjs`; watch for noisy matches as
  contracts spread beyond curated notes.
- Two artifacts can now carry overlapping contracts for the same change
  surface; the `/clean` distillation step is the place to spot and merge
  duplicates.
- Recall quality differs between qmd and non-qmd machines for the same gate;
  the stderr notice surfaces this but does not remove it.

documents.title: ADR: Narrow GP3 staleness to active tasks; exempt terminal status and x_evergreen
documents.text:
decision_adr-narrow-staleness-to-tasks ADR: Narrow GP3 staleness to active tasks; exempt terminal status and x_evergreen content/decisions/decision_adr-narrow-staleness-to-tasks.md decision active team Operations Documentation decision_adr-task-done-vs-archived-lif playbook_golden-principles doc:content/playbooks/playbook_golden-principles.md doc:content/tasks/2026/04/task_decide-gp3-staleness-scope.md doc:content/decisions/decision_adr-task-done-vs-archived-lif.md ## Context

Golden Principle 3 ("Keep Artifacts Fresh") fires a >90-day staleness
warning on every artifact regardless of type or status. As of
2026-04-27 this produces ~274 warnings out of 279 total — almost
entirely from 2025-era research notes, legal references, meeting
records, and other frozen reference material. The signal-to-noise
ratio is so low that genuine staleness on active tasks is
undetectable.

The 2026-04-24 `/review-principles` pass surfaced this. The triage
question that followed: *"do notes have expiry? they are not to-do's
or something."*

Two related decisions inform the scope:

- `decision_adr-task-done-vs-archived-lif` ratifies that `done`,
  `archived`, and `cancelled` are *terminal* lifecycle outcomes.
  Terminal tasks are closed and not expected to be updated, so
  staleness on them is pure noise.
- The lifecycle ADR also forbids age-based status flips, so the
  cleanup pathway "archive stale done tasks to silence warnings" is
  off the table. The validator must do the right thing on its own.

## Decision

GP3's staleness check applies only when ALL of the following hold:

1. `artifact.type === 'task'`
2. `artifact.frontmatter.status NOT IN { done, archived, cancelled }`
3. `artifact.frontmatter.x_evergreen !== true`

Equivalently:

- **Notes, decisions, meetings, initiatives, playbooks, and other
  non-task artifacts are never flagged as stale.** They capture
  moments or rules; they do not rot on a clock.
- **Terminal-status tasks are never flagged as stale.** Closure is the
  signal; an `updated_at` from six months ago is the *correct* state
  for a finished task.
- **`x_evergreen: true` is the explicit per-artifact opt-out** for
  non-terminal tasks that legitimately span multiple quarters
  (multi-month initiatives, on-call playbooks-as-tasks, long-running
  monitoring tickets).

The 90-day threshold itself is unchanged.

## Implementation

- `scripts/lib/validate.mjs` `validateFreshness()` skips the check
  when any of the three conditions above is true.
- `scripts/lib/audit.mjs` applies the same skip rules when collecting
  `staleArtifacts` for the audit grade. *(2026-08-10: audit.mjs retired by
  [`decision_adr-retire-letter-grade-audit`](decision_adr-retire-letter-grade-audit.md);
  the skip rules now live only in `validate.mjs`, which this ADR continues
  to govern.)*
- `content/playbooks/playbook_golden-principles.md` GP3 is updated to
  state the narrowed scope, the terminal-status exemption, and the
  `x_evergreen` escape hatch.
- `frontmatter-schema.mjs` already accepts arbitrary `x_*` extension
  fields, so no schema change is needed for `x_evergreen`.

## Consequences

- Validator output drops from ~279 warnings to ~5 (the existing
  unknown-`superseded_by` warnings on archived tasks, plus any
  genuinely stale active tasks).
- Audit grade for `note`, `meeting`, `playbook`, `initiative`, and
  `decision` types is no longer dragged down by the staleness penalty.
  The `task` grade is bounded by active tasks, which is the right
  signal.
- Future long-running active tasks (e.g., `task_full-risk-review-execution`,
  multi-quarter initiative trackers) MAY mark themselves
  `x_evergreen: true` to opt out of the freshness clock without
  changing status.
- The historical pattern of "stale notes drown the validate stream"
  ends. `/review-principles` can rely on validator output as a
  high-signal triage surface again.

## Alternatives Considered

### Keep GP3 universal, encourage manual archival of stale notes

Rejected. Manual archival of frozen reference material would either
relabel `done` → `archived` (forbidden by
`decision_adr-task-done-vs-archived-lif`) or move legitimate active
reference notes to `status: archived`, which lies about their
applicability. Both fixes are worse than the noise.

### Narrow to tasks but exempt only `archived`, not all terminal statuses

Rejected. Lifecycle ADR treats `done`, `archived`, and `cancelled` as
equally terminal. Exempting only `archived` would push the team back
toward the forbidden age-based relabeling.

### Drop GP3 entirely

Rejected. Active tasks really do rot. Stale `active` tasks (no
update in 90+ days) are a useful warning that priorities have moved
on without closing the task. Keeping the check on this slice only
recovers the original intent.

### Make `x_evergreen` a general flag (also excludes from audit grading, search boosting, etc.)

Deferred. This ADR scopes `x_evergreen` to staleness only. Adding
broader semantics is a separate decision when a concrete need lands.

documents.title: ADR: Retire the letter-grade entropy audit (hey audit)
documents.text:
decision_adr-retire-letter-grade-audit ADR: Retire the letter-grade entropy audit (hey audit) content/decisions/decision_adr-retire-letter-grade-audit.md decision Team active team Engineering Operations decision_slug-ids-and-letter-grades decision_adr-narrow-staleness-to-tasks doc:content/decisions/decision_slug-ids-and-letter-grades.md doc:content/decisions/decision_adr-loop-control-driver-surface.md ## Context

`./hey audit` graded every content artifact on a 9-point frontmatter-shape
score (sources, entities, tags, freshness, body length, feedback, relations)
and reported letter grades per artifact, per type, and overall. It was wired
into `/clean`, `/sync`, `/validate`, `/assess`, and the agent quick-reference
tables.

A 2026-08-10 review measured what it actually produced over the full
2,562-artifact corpus:

- **A dead dimension.** The feedback input was a permanent stub
  (`feedbackAgg = {}` — "placeholder until feedback artifact type is
  implemented"), so `no feedback` fired on 2,562/2,562 artifacts and every
  artifact unconditionally lost 1 of 9 points. A+ (9/9) was mathematically
  unreachable; the repo contained zero A+ artifacts.
- **Checks measured unadopted conventions, not quality.** `no entities
  tagged` fired on 94.5% of artifacts, `no outgoing relations` on 41%,
  `no sources` on 39%. A check that ~everything fails describes the
  convention's adoption, not any artifact's quality.
- **Unactionable output.** 659 artifacts (26%) graded C or below; `/clean`
  instructed flagging them. A 659-item list is a list nobody fixes.
- **No behavioral trace.** In four months, no commit tuned the grading
  criteria, and no log, note, or task cites an audit grade as the reason for
  any action.
- **The one real signal was redundant.** The stale list (61 open tasks with
  `updated_at` > 90 days) decomposed exactly into 60 undated tasks — already
  surfaced by the loop board's undated pile
  ([`decision_adr-loop-control-driver-surface`](decision_adr-loop-control-driver-surface.md))
  — plus 1 overdue task, already caught by session-start overdue triage.
  The validation section literally re-ran `./hey validate`.

## Decision

Remove the letter-grade audit wholesale; absorb nothing, because every
non-redundant output already has a better-owned surface:

1. **Delete** `scripts/lib/audit.mjs` and the `./hey audit` command.
2. **`/assess` Health** reports validation state only (errors/warnings via
   `validateRepository`); audit grade, quality distribution, and stale count
   are dropped.
3. **Ceremonies** (`/clean`, `/sync`, `/validate`) and agent docs
   (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md`) drop their audit steps and
   references. Artifact-quality pressure stays where it is actionable:
   `./hey validate` (structural correctness, hard gate), the loop board
   undated pile (rotting-task attention), and session-start overdue triage.
4. **Task-scoped staleness semantics survive** — `isStalenessExempt` lives in
   `validate.mjs` and
   [`decision_adr-narrow-staleness-to-tasks`](decision_adr-narrow-staleness-to-tasks.md)
   continues to govern it; only its audit-side consumer is gone.
5. [`decision_slug-ids-and-letter-grades`](decision_slug-ids-and-letter-grades.md)
   is **partially superseded**: its letter-grade half is retired by this ADR;
   its slug-ID half remains fully in force.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Fix the metric** (remove the dead feedback dimension, drop the entities
   check, recalibrate thresholds). Rejected: it makes a report nobody reads
   more accurate. Four months of zero behavioral trace is evidence of absent
   demand, not miscalibration.
2. **Keep only the stale list.** Rejected: measured overlap was total
   (60 undated + 1 overdue of 61); a second surface for the same tasks is
   drift waiting to happen.
3. **Keep the command undocumented.** Rejected: dead-but-invocable code paths
   still cost maintenance (the module imported the validator and staleness
   rules) and mislead new members.

## Consequences

### Positive

- Four ceremony surfaces lose a step that produced no decisions; agent docs
  shrink.
- No more unearnable grade dimension silently deflating every artifact.
- Quality signals consolidate onto surfaces with forced action: validator
  errors block, overdue triage demands a verdict per task, the undated pile
  is scored per owner.

### Negative

- Cross-cutting metadata coverage (entities/relations/sources density) loses
  its only aggregate view. If a real consumer for that appears, it should be
  rebuilt against a *lived* convention and a named reader, not resurrected
  as-is.
- `/assess` Health is thinner (validation only); period-over-period quality
  trends were never captured anyway.

documents.title: Slug-based IDs and letter-only audit grades
documents.text:
decision_slug-ids-and-letter-grades Slug-based IDs and letter-only audit grades content/decisions/decision_slug-ids-and-letter-grades.md decision team Operations decision_deflate-ontology doc:docs/SPEC.md doc:AGENTS.md ## Context

The original artifact ID format used 26-character ULIDs (e.g. `dec_01KJVT2Y6EWG1NGC3TP7KCEZFJ`). These were machine-friendly but imposed cognitive burden on humans reading filenames, relations, and cross-references. The audit system reported quality as numerical percentages (e.g. "72%") that conveyed false precision — the underlying score is just 0-9 discrete points.

## Decision

### 1. Slug-based IDs

Replace ULID-based artifact IDs with human-readable slug-based IDs.

- Format: `{prefix}_{slug}` (e.g. `dec_deflate-ontology`)
- Slug: max 30 chars, lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens, auto-derived from title at creation
- Filenames: `{id}.md` (no redundant slug duplication)
- Uniqueness enforced by validator; collisions resolved by appending `-2`, `-3`

### 2. Letter-only audit grades

> **Superseded 2026-08-10** by
> [`decision_adr-retire-letter-grade-audit`](decision_adr-retire-letter-grade-audit.md):
> the letter-grade audit itself is retired (`./hey audit` and
> `scripts/lib/audit.mjs` removed), so this section no longer governs
> anything. Section 1 (slug-based IDs) remains fully in force.

Replace numerical percentages with letter grades.

| Grade | Score |
|-------|-------|
| A+ | 9/9 (perfect) |
| A | 7-8/9 |
| B | 5-6/9 |
| C | 3-4/9 |
| D | 1-2/9 |
| F | 0/9 |

No percentages appear in CLI or JSON output.

## Consequences

- IDs are readable at a glance in filenames, relations, and git logs
- Relations like `target: tsk_bootstrap-kb` are self-documenting
- Audit output is cleaner and avoids false-precision percentages
- Trade-off: slugs are set at creation time and won't track title renames (acceptable — same pattern as URL slugs)
- Trade-off: IDs lose temporal ordering that ULIDs provided (acceptable — `created_at` serves this purpose)

documents.title: Golden Principles: Keep the Repo Clean
documents.text:
playbook_golden-principles Golden Principles: Keep the Repo Clean content/playbooks/playbook_golden-principles.md playbook active team Operations Review decision_deflate-ontology playbook_operating-philosophy playbook_governing-artifact-maintenance doc:content/policies/governance.yml doc:AGENTS.md # Golden Principles: Keep the Repo Clean

Practical rules to keep knowledge legible, consistent, and useful. Apply at write time, not as an audit gate — `./hey validate` is the only mechanical check; the rest is writer discipline. A retrospective review pass is opt-in for cross-file refactors or ontology shifts.

## Principle 1: No Unattributed Claims

Decision artifacts must include `sources`. Unsourced claims belong in a `note` with a hypothesis tag.

**Enforced by:** `./hey validate` (sources policy in `governance.yml`)

## Principle 2: Use Shared Vocabulary

Use terms from `content/vocab/entities.yml` and `content/vocab/tags.yml`. Add new terms to vocab first, then use them.

**Enforced by:** `./hey validate` (tag and entity vocabulary checks)

## Principle 3: Keep Active Tasks Fresh

Review *active tasks* stale >90 days. Update them, close them, or mark them `x_evergreen: true` to prevent priorities from drifting unnoticed.

Scope (per [`decision_adr-narrow-staleness-to-tasks`](../decisions/decision_adr-narrow-staleness-to-tasks.md)):

- Applies to `type: task` only. Notes, decisions, meetings, initiatives, and playbooks are not on a freshness clock — they capture moments or rules, not open work.
- Terminal-status tasks (`done`, `archived`, `cancelled`) are exempt. Closure is the signal; the `updated_at` of a finished task is *supposed* to be old. Per [`decision_adr-task-done-vs-archived-lif`](../decisions/decision_adr-task-done-vs-archived-lif.md), do not relabel `done` → `archived` based on age.
- Long-running active tasks that legitimately span multiple quarters (multi-month initiatives, on-call playbooks-as-tasks, long-running monitoring tickets) MAY set frontmatter `x_evergreen: true` to opt out explicitly.

Freshness also applies to governing artifacts. If a change alters team behavior, routing, or policy, the artifact that governs that behavior MUST be updated in the same work — but this is a discipline expectation enforced at PR review, not by the staleness clock.

**Enforced by:** `./hey validate` (staleness detection scoped per [`decision_adr-narrow-staleness-to-tasks`](../decisions/decision_adr-narrow-staleness-to-tasks.md), 90-day threshold)

## Principle 4: One Artifact, One Concern

Each artifact covers a single topic. If a task exceeds 3 acceptance criteria, split it.

**Enforced by:** Convention (review during PR)

## Principle 5: Relations Over Duplication

Don’t copy information across artifacts. Link it via `relations` (e.g., `supports`, `implements`, `links_to`).

**Enforced by:** `./hey validate` (relation target integrity)

## Principle 6: Sources Chain Completeness

Decisions link to prompting tasks. Tasks link to authorizing decisions. Build a navigable graph.

**Enforced by:** Convention (the letter-grade relation-density check was retired by [`decision_adr-retire-letter-grade-audit`](../decisions/decision_adr-retire-letter-grade-audit.md))

## Principle 7: Canonical Before Custom

Prefer existing entities/tags in `content/vocab/`. Use aliases in `entities.yml` when appropriate.

**Enforced by:** `./hey validate` (entity vocabulary checks)

## Periodic Maintenance

Run `./hey validate` weekly (the `/clean` checklist wraps it) to review
validation errors/warnings and vocab compliance. Rotting open tasks surface
through the loop board's undated pile and session-start overdue triage — not
a separate grade report (see
[`decision_adr-retire-letter-grade-audit`](../decisions/decision_adr-retire-letter-grade-audit.md)).

During change-intent work, use `playbook_governing-artifact-maintenance` as the input and output hook for keeping rules synchronized with behavior.

documents.title: ADR: Loop control is the driver surface; tasks, packets, and logs stay as ledgers
documents.text:
decision_adr-loop-control-driver-surface ADR: Loop control is the driver surface; tasks, packets, and logs stay as ledgers content/decisions/decision_adr-loop-control-driver-surface.md decision Team team Operations Automation Documentation doc:workspace/charlie/ideas/2026-04-30-idea-loop-control-workflow-candidate.md doc:workspace/charlie/ideas/2026-04-30-idea-scheduled-action-packets.md doc:content/playbooks/playbook_loop-control-usage-guide.md ## Context

The repo has many ledgers. Tasks hold committed work state. Notes and
playbooks hold durable context. Inbox items hold raw intake and
handoffs. Logs hold transient continuity. Git holds validated change
boundaries. Scheduled action packets hold time-triggered prompts.

These ledgers are pastward and present-tense by construction. Logs
record what happened. Tasks record what is committed. Inbox records
what arrived. None of them, on their own, answer the live question
the human driver actually asks every morning: **"What needs my
attention now, what is moving without me, and what is coming?"**

In April–May 2026 we tried to answer this two ways:

1. **Read everything**: scan the whole `content/tasks/` tree, today's
   commits, the inbox, every running agent. This works for a small
   day; it collapses at any real load. It also pulls the driver into
   transcript granularity (which file? which run? which command?)
   when the actual driver decision is at lane granularity (decide /
   unblock / review / ignore).

2. **Trust the daily log**: lean on `workspace/{member}/logs/` as the
   primary surface. This fails for the opposite reason: logs are
   append-only and pastward. They cannot, by construction, project
   work that hasn't happened yet. The cliff symptom is visible on
   2026-05-27, where eight overdue tasks were blanket-deferred to a
   single future date (`2026-06-05`) — because there was no
   graduated forward view, every "not now" item collapsed onto one
   horizon.

Both failure modes share a cause: the driver was asked to compute the
attention lane themselves, instead of being handed it.

## Decision

**The loop is the driver's primary surface. The ledgers (tasks,
notes, inbox, logs, packets, git) remain the source of truth. The
loop is a projection over them; it stores no durable state of its
own.**

### Three projections, one surface

| Projection | Axis | Answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `./hey loop brief` | summary | "What is in flight, what is overdue, what changed since I last looked?" |
| `./hey loop board` | attention lane | "What needs decision / unblock / review / attention right now?" |
| `./hey loop horizon` | due-date window | "What lands today, this week, next week, in two weeks, in a month?" *(2026-08-14: also iteration buckets — see [`decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline`](./decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline.md))* |

`brief` is the short scan. `board` is the present-tense attention
view. `horizon` is the forward-tense prospect view. The three are
deliberately separate — combining them produces a wall of detail no
one reads.

### Four driver attention lanes (and what they each demand)

| Lane | Trigger | Driver verb |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Needs decision | judgment cannot be deferred to code, doc, or agent | decide, ask, delegate |
| Needs unblock | dependency, owner, conflict, or input is missing | unblock or reroute |
| Needs review | output exists, awaits human signal | review or assign reviewer |
| Needs attention | overdue, stale, or invalid state | triage or refresh |

Lanes derive from `status`, `phase`, `blocked_by` relations, due
date, and run state. They are not a new field. If the derivation
misses real intent, fix the derivation rule — do not add
`x_attention` as a manual override. The lane is the *output* of the
ledger state, never the input.

### Packets carry future prompts, not future work

A scheduled action packet says *"re-surface this at time T."* It is
not a task. The boundary:

- If the future moment requires substantive work, **create a task**
  with a `due_date`. The horizon projection will surface it.
  *(2026-08-14: superseded in part — commit the task to an `iteration`
  instead; `due_date` only for hard external deadlines, per
  [`decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline`](./decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline.md).)*
- If the future moment is a reminder, light check, or
  agent-readable follow-up, **create a packet**. It surfaces in the
  brief (when due) and horizon (always).
- A packet may *point* to a task. A packet must not *replace* one.

This boundary is the reason packets are not a "second task system."
Treating them as one collapses the distinction the loop relies on.

### The loop carries no state the ledgers don't

The brief, board, and horizon are recomputed every time they run.
There is no `loop.db`, no `attention.json`, no checkpoint file. This
is enforced by composition: every projection is a function of
manifest + inbox + packet list + run attempts, all of which live in
git or in workspace files. If you delete the loop tooling tomorrow,
no information is lost.

This rule is what lets us evolve the lane derivation, add new
projections (like horizon), and change formatting without migrating
data.

## Consequences

### Positive

- The driver scans lanes and windows, not transcripts. The cost of
  morning routine becomes O(lanes + horizon buckets), not O(tasks).
- Forward visibility is no longer dependent on memory or grep.
  Horizon makes "due in 14 days" a first-class view.
- The ledgers remain authoritative. Promoting an idea, closing a
  task, sending an inbox item — all still produce immediate loop
  effects because the loop reads them directly.
- Adding a projection is cheap. `loop horizon` (2026-05-27) added
  two functions and one subcommand; no schema changes, no
  migrations.

### Negative

- Derived lanes mean the driver sometimes disagrees with the
  derivation ("this is not really blocked, the blocker is stale").
  The fix is to clean the ledger (close stale blockers, refresh
  `updated_at`, fix invalid `phase`), not to override the lane.
- Horizon quality is exactly as good as `due_date` hygiene. The
  `No due date` bucket on 2026-05-27 contains 41 tasks. That pile
  is a forcing function — it makes the gap visible — but it is
  also a reminder that "the tool only works if the inputs are
  clean."
- Three commands instead of one. The morning routine runs `brief`,
  `board`, `horizon`. We accept this as cheaper than one
  ever-growing wall.

### Out of scope (explicitly)

- The loop does not claim, mutate, or close tasks. Those go through
  `./hey work claim`, the task body, or `./hey inbox`.
- The loop does not run agents. Agent execution is the harness
  domain (`initiative_harness-v1-execution-harness`).
- The loop does not write to the daily log. The daily log is
  authored by `/morning`, `/snap`, `/night`; the loop is a read
  surface those skills consume.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **One mega-board with lanes and a time axis** — rejected.
   Combining attention and horizon produces a 2D grid no one reads
   on a phone or in Slack. Two separate views are easier to scan
   and easier to evolve independently.

2. **A persistent attention store with an `x_attention` field on
   every task** — rejected. Adds a new field that gets stale, needs
   migration, and lets the ledger and the loop disagree. Derivation
   from existing fields keeps the loop honest.

3. **Treat packets as tasks with `kind: reminder`** — rejected. The
   "if it's real work, make it a task" rule depends on packets being
   structurally different. Unifying them dilutes the rule and turns
   packets into a backdoor for noise.

4. **Auto-populate the daily log with horizon data on every
   `/snap`** — rejected for now. The log is pastward; injecting
   forward data into it duplicates state and confuses the
   audit trail. The loop is read on demand; the log records what
   happened with it.

## Amendment (2026-08-14)

Per D2 of
`note_automated-initiative-task-hygiene-strategy`
(charlie pilot):

- **Fisher may author scaffold sections** of ceremonies and daily
  logs — clearly marked, containing pastward facts only: commits,
  activity, run outcomes. It may also precompute digests (morning
  brief, iteration pre-package). The "out of scope" rule above is
  narrowed accordingly: the mechanical half of `/morning`, `/snap`,
  `/night` may be Fisher-written.
- **Judgment lines remain member-authored.** Reflections, decisions,
  priorities, archival — never Fisher.
- **The alternative-4 rejection stands, narrowed to forward-tense
  data.** It targeted injecting *forward* (horizon) data into a
  pastward log, and that stays rejected: forward data lives in the
  digest, never the log. Pastward-fact scaffolds record what
  happened — exactly what the log is for.
- **Packets are consumed by the morning digest**, restoring the
  re-surfacing loop.

## Amendment (2026-08-19) — "never the log" is superseded by the removal of `digests/`

The 2026-08-14 amendment above held that **forward data lives in the digest,
never the log**. That rule is retired, because its premise no longer exists:
charlie removed the `digests/` directory, and `workspace/<member>/logs/YYYY-MM-DD.md`
is now the single durable record. A rule that routes forward data to a home that
was deleted has no referent — it does not constrain, it just fails.

The *concern* behind alternative 4 was never location. It was that injecting
machine-written forward state into a member-authored pastward record duplicates
state and confuses the audit trail. That concern is preserved by ownership
rather than by separate files:

- The scheduled `loop digest --record` pass writes **only** between
  `<!-- fisher:digest:start -->` and `<!-- fisher:digest:end -->`, alongside the
  scaffold's own marker pair. Each unattended writer owns one region and nothing
  else, so machine-written and member-written content stay separable inside one
  file.
- The digest section is explicitly labelled a forward-looking projection and
  machine-owned, and it **never emits a `## Plan`**. A plan is a commitment, and
  commitments remain member-authored — the "judgment lines remain
  member-authored" rule is unchanged and is what this preserves.

**Why the change was needed at all.** With an ephemeral delivery as its only
output, the pass left the repo unable to answer *"did management run today?"*.
That question is the whole point of the ceremony crons, and it must be
answerable without invoking `/morning` or reading `hermes cron list` — both of
which are themselves rituals, and rituals are the failure mode the 2026-W33
retrospective identified. A log carrying the digest section but no `## Plan` is
now a precise, readable statement: the machine ran, the member has not committed
to a day. The 21:30 double-check in `workspace/fisher/ceremony-crons.md` reads
exactly that distinction.

## Relations

- Promotes the rationale from
  [`note_2026-04-30-loop-control-workflow-candidate`](../../workspace/charlie/ideas/2026-04-30-idea-loop-control-workflow-candidate.md)
  and
  [`note_2026-04-30-scheduled-action-packets`](../../workspace/charlie/ideas/2026-04-30-idea-scheduled-action-packets.md)
  into a permanent team ADR.
- Operational usage lives in
  [`playbook_loop-control-usage-guide`](../playbooks/playbook_loop-control-usage-guide.md).
- Lane derivation references the priority semantics in
  [`decision_adr-replace-p0-p3-priority-wit`](./decision_adr-replace-p0-p3-priority-wit.md).

documents.title: ADR: Three-layer task timeline — due_date is the alarm, iteration is the commitment, x_planned_date is the schedule
documents.text:
decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline ADR: Three-layer task timeline — due_date is the alarm, iteration is the commitment, x_planned_date is the schedule content/decisions/decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline.md decision active team Operations Automation Documentation decision_adr-loop-control-driver-surface decision_adr-replace-p0-p3-priority-wit doc:content/notes/2026/08/note_automated-initiative-task-hygiene-strategy.md user_request:chat:2026-08-14-task-timeline-and-hygiene-design ## Context

Measured on 2026-08-14 (`./hey db query`):

- 307 open tasks; 201 (65%) with no `due_date`, invisible to
  `loop horizon`.
- 24 overdue (oldest 2026-04-24); 21 tasks "due today"; 163 open
  tasks untouched for 30+ days.

One field — `due_date` — carried three meanings: external deadline,
self-schedule, and wish. All three shared a single alarm semantic.
21 tasks "due today" is not a schedule. The cliff-defer pathology
documented in
[`decision_adr-loop-control-driver-surface`](decision_adr-loop-control-driver-surface.md)
(2026-05-27, eight tasks blanket-deferred to one date) recurred.
Session-start triage costs one human decision per overdue item; that
does not survive 24 items — people skip or blanket-defer, which
regrows the pile.

Ratified in-session by charlie on 2026-08-14 as decisions D1, D3,
and D4 of
`note_automated-initiative-task-hygiene-strategy`.
This ADR is the durable record.

## Decision

Split the one overloaded field into three layers with distinct
semantics. The human-perceivable timeline unit is the iteration
(week), not the date.

### Three Layers

| Field | Meaning | Overdue semantics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `due_date` | Hard external deadline (launch, partner commitment, meeting) | Yes — real alarm; daily triage |
| `iteration: YYYY-WNN` | Weekly commitment, cap 10 per member | No — unfinished work carries forward with a slip count |
| `x_planned_date` | Weekday schedule inside the iteration | None — a missed plan returns to the iteration's unplanned pool |

- `due_date` is the only layer with overdue semantics. It stays in
  daily session-start triage, which becomes small by construction.
- `iteration` is what a member commits to this week. The cap applies
  to iteration membership only; Eisenhower `priority` keeps its
  semantics from
  [`decision_adr-replace-p0-p3-priority-wit`](decision_adr-replace-p0-p3-priority-wit.md)
  unchanged.
- `x_planned_date` is schedule, not deadline. Schedule is cheap to
  move; deadline is expensive to move. The morning view leads with
  today's planned set.

### Field Semantics

Presence of a field carries the meaning. No flag to forget.

- `due_date` present ⇒ external commitment. Alarm on overdue.
- No `due_date`, `iteration` present ⇒ this week's commitment.
- Neither ⇒ backlog.

### Automatic Carry

Ratifies D3. At the iteration boundary (`./hey iteration carry`,
run at `iteration-turn`):

- Unfinished committed tasks carry forward mechanically — no
  per-batch approval. Carry is information-preserving and
  reversible; requiring approval would recreate the pile this design
  removes.
- `x_slip_count` increments on each carry. It is written only by the
  mechanism, never by hand — ledger input, consistent with the
  loop-control ADR's no-`x_attention` rule.
- At `x_slip_count >= 3` the task blocks the ceremony until the
  member decides: re-scope, re-commit with a reason, or archive.
  Blanket carry is not cliff-defer redux because slips are counted
  and forced to a decision.

### Parameters

Ratifies D4. Defaults, tuned from operation, not upfront:

- Weekly commitment cap: 10 per member.

### Backlog health: the definition, and the one number (2026-08-19)

The retired metric was *"count of open tasks with no `due_date`, hold it below
N"*. It is not merely failed, it is invalid: this ADR makes no-due-date the
**normal** backlog state, so the number falls when wish-dates are stripped and
rises when they are added, and moves for reasons unrelated to health. On
2026-08-19, stripping 39 wish-dates took charlie's hard-deadline overdue count
from 45 to 0 without a single task closing — proof the old number measured
conformance to a replaced model.

**Definition.** Backlog health is whether the layer that carries the work is
honest. Under this ADR that layer is the **weekly commitment**, not the date.
An iteration holding many times its cap is not a commitment; it is a list, and
the iteration view built on it is decorative.

**The one number to hold: committed vs cap — open tasks in the current
iteration, per member, against the cap of 10.** Read
`./hey loop health`; it is also printed by `./hey validate`, which runs
unattended on every write.

Deliberately *not* the number:

- **`x_planned_date` coverage.** The schedule layer is an optional override.
  Making coverage the metric would re-create on `x_planned_date` exactly the
  pressure this ADR removed from `due_date`. It is reported as a diagnostic and
  can never fail the check.
- **Backlog size.** A large backlog with no iteration tag is the healthy resting
  state. Nothing about it is debt.

Companion signals, reported alongside but subordinate: `x_slip_count >= 3`
(chronic carry, already gated at the ceremony) and the digest heartbeat, whose
budget is one day — the daily log is the tracked evidence that the scheduled
pass ran, and a stall is reported as the automation stopping rather than as a
skipped day.
- Slip decision threshold: 3.
- `doing` demotion window: 14 days (hygiene check).

### Migration

One-time, batch:

- Open tasks untouched 30+ days lose `due_date` mechanically and
  move to backlog. No per-item decisions.
- Future-dated `due_date` values need member confirmation before
  stripping — some are genuine external deadlines.
- The remainder gets one batch triage pass at the next
  `iteration-turn`: commit to an iteration, keep the date (hard
  deadline only), or backlog.

## Implementation

Landed 2026-08-14, commit `15f41cd01`:

- `./hey iteration carry` — carry plan, `x_slip_count` increment,
  slip-threshold gate (`scripts/lib/iteration-carry.mjs`).
- `./hey hygiene check` — read-only batch detector
  (`scripts/lib/hygiene.mjs`).
- `loop horizon` gained iteration buckets (this / next / backlog),
  sorted `x_planned_date`-first — the precondition before wish-dates
  are stripped.
- Schema checks: `x_slip_count` integer ≥ 0, `x_planned_date`
  ISO date (`scripts/lib/frontmatter-schema.mjs`).

## Consequences

### Positive

- Daily triage shrinks to hard-deadline overdues, small by
  construction.
- The forward view is "my ~10 commitments", not 300 dates.
- Chronic slippage becomes a visible number (`x_slip_count`) instead
  of an invisible habit, with a forced decision at 3.

### Negative

- One-time migration cost, and a confirmation pass for future-dated
  wish-dates.
- `x_planned_date` discipline is a new habit; the cap needs an
  enforcement surface at `iteration-turn`.
- Horizon date buckets go quiet for most tasks; the iteration
  buckets replace them as the primary forward view.

### Out of scope

- Hygiene-check rule details (strategy note P2).
- Fisher ceremony scaffolds (P3/D2 — amendment to the loop-control
  ADR, not this one).
- Packet-loop absorption details (P4) and duplicate merging.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Single `due_date` plus an `x_hard_deadline` flag** — rejected.
   A forgotten flag leaks noise (wish-date alarms) or silence
   (missed real deadline). Presence-of-field semantics fail safe.

2. **Remove dates entirely; iteration-only** — rejected. Members do
   plan weekdays, and external deadlines are real alarms. The fix is
   splitting the meanings, not removing dates.

3. **Keep per-item daily triage with better discipline** — rejected.
   One decision per item does not survive 24 items; the observed
   response is skipping or blanket-defer, which regrows the pile.

4. **Packets as the anti-cliff-defer device** — superseded.
   Re-surfacing deferred tasks moves to the carry mechanism; the
   packet loop had been dead for two months. Packets remain for
   genuine one-off reminders.

documents.text:
playbook_loop-control-usage-guide Loop Control Usage Guide content/playbooks/playbook_loop-control-usage-guide.md playbook Team active team Operations Documentation Automation doc:workspace/charlie/ideas/2026-04-30-idea-loop-control-workflow-candidate.md doc:workspace/charlie/ideas/2026-04-30-idea-scheduled-action-packets.md doc:content/initiatives/2026/05/initiative_harness-v1-execution-harness.md user_request:codex-2026-08-25-morning-hierarchy doc:workspace/charlie/logs/2026-08-25.md # Loop Control Usage Guide

## Purpose

Use the loop to drive many tasks, packets, and agent runs without reading every detail every time.

The loop is a projection over repo state. It is not a second task system.

## Core Rule

The human driver MUST track lanes and interventions, not every event.

The repo remains the ledger:

- Tasks hold committed work state.
- Notes and playbooks hold durable context.
- Inbox items hold raw intake and handoffs.
- Scheduled action packets hold time-triggered prompts.
- Mission packs hold task execution context for agents.
- Git commits hold validated change boundaries.

## Daily Shape

### Morning

Start from the control surface:

```bash
MORNING_DATE="$(TZ=Asia/Seoul date +%F)"
git pull --rebase --autostash origin main
./hey index build
./hey db build
./hey loop brief --member <member> --today "$MORNING_DATE"
./hey loop board --member <member> --today "$MORNING_DATE"
./hey loop horizon --member <member> --today "$MORNING_DATE"
```

Use `brief` for the short scan. Use `board` to choose focus.

The morning pass MUST bind every projection and log path to the same KST calendar date. Pass `--today` explicitly; do not let an early-morning UTC date choose the previous day's plan.

Morning focus SHOULD come from this order:

1. `Needs decision`
2. `Needs unblock`
3. `Needs review`
4. due scheduled action packets
5. active or failed agent runs
6. stale `Needs attention`
7. `Ready queue`

#### Daily Plan Hierarchy

The member-authored `## Plan` MUST use three semantic levels:

1. `###` — a large topic: one observable outcome for the day.
2. `####` — a middle topic: one decision, unblock, review, or execution stream.
3. A column-zero `- [ ]` line — a small topic: one atomic next action.

Use this shape:

```markdown
## Plan

### 1. Large Topic

**Today's outcome:** One observable result.

#### 1.1 Middle Topic

- [ ] **1.1.a Small action** (`task_id`, lane, priority) — Next: verb + object. Done: evidence or ledger state.
```

Apply these rules:

- Keep the plan to about three large topics and seven small actions. Add more only when a hard deadline or driver lane would otherwise disappear.
- A small action tied to tracked work MUST include its task ID. Use `[operating decision]` when no task exists.
- Include lane, priority, or hard deadline only when it changes execution order.
- State both the next action and the completion evidence on one line.
- Mention each task once. Other sections SHOULD reference the plan number instead of duplicating the task text.
- Do not put another `##` heading inside `## Plan`; `/snap` and log compaction treat the next level-two heading as the end of the plan.
- Preserve Fisher-owned marker regions exactly. Human-authored priorities MUST stay outside those regions.

See [`workspace/charlie/logs/2026-08-25.md`](../../workspace/charlie/logs/2026-08-25.md) for a worked example.

### Snap

Use `/snap` to record a control-state checkpoint:

```bash
./hey loop brief --member <member>
./hey loop board --member <member>
```

The snap should answer:

- What is in flight?
- What changed lanes?
- Did any packet become due or get handled?
- Did an agent run fail, finish, or need review?
- What should the next driver do?

If a task is ready for agent execution, compile the mission before handoff:

```bash
./hey mission compile --task <task_id>
```

### Night

Close the day from the loop board:

```bash
./hey loop brief --member <member>
./hey loop board --member <member>
./hey packet list --member <member> --include-future
```

Night reflection SHOULD convert open loop lanes into one of:

- tomorrow's priority
- blocker to unblock
- review item
- scheduled action packet
- task or note update
- safe background

## Agent Handoff

Before assigning a task to an AI agent, compile a mission:

```bash
./hey mission compile --task <task_id>
```

Give the agent the generated `mission.md` or `mission.json`.

The mission SHOULD define:

- task context
- definition of done
- related artifacts
- dependency obligations
- evidence checklist
- escalation boundary
- runtime targets

If multiple agents work on one task, keep one canonical task and split runs by role:

| Role | Scope |
| --- | --- |
| Explorer | read-only context mapping |
| Worker | scoped implementation |
| Reviewer | risks and findings |
| Verifier | validation evidence |

Same-task agents MUST have explicit write scopes before they modify files.

## Scheduled Packets

Create a packet when a future prompt should re-enter the loop:

```bash
./hey packet new \
  --workspace <member> \
  --title "Review loop control board" \
  --trigger-at 2026-05-13 \
  --audience <member> \
  --action "Review whether the board lanes changed today's driver decisions."
```

Use packets for:

- reminders
- lightweight checks
- review prompts
- small artifact updates with clear instructions
- agent-readable follow-ups

Do not use packets for substantial work. Create a task for substantial work and let the packet point to the task.

Packets are for genuine one-off reminders. Re-surfacing deferred tasks is the iteration carry mechanism's job, not a packet's ([`decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline`](../decisions/decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline.md)).

## Write-Back

Every loop pass should write back only the state that matters.

Use this handoff shape when closing a task, snap, or agent run:

```markdown
## Loop Handoff

- Changed:
- Why:
- Validation:
- Risk:
- Next:
```

Write it where the next reader will look:

| Situation | Write-back location |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical task state changed | task body |
| Personal continuity changed | `workspace/<member>/logs/` |
| Another member needs action | `./hey inbox send` |
| Future prompt is needed | `./hey packet new` |
| Agent needs execution context | `./hey mission compile` |

## What Not To Do

- Do not treat the board as source of truth.
- Do not create a packet when a task is needed.
- Do not list healthy background runs as driver work.
- Do not ask the human to read every run transcript.
- Do not let two writer agents edit the same files without explicit scope.
- Do not close a loop pass without updating the task, note, packet, log, or commit that carries the state forward.

## Troubleshooting

If the board feels noisy, look for stale task status, missing blockers, vague task titles, or old `updated_at` values.

If an agent is confused, compile or refresh the mission and check whether the task has a clear definition of done.

If a due packet keeps reappearing, either complete it, convert it to a task, change its trigger, or mark it stale in the packet note.

If two agents disagree, keep both results attached to the same task until the driver selects the canonical path.

documents.text:
decision_adr-kg-v2-operating-decisions ADR: Knowledge Graph v2 operating decisions — procedure representation, gate policy, agent identity, links_to deprecation, auditor export, registry upkeep content/decisions/decision_adr-kg-v2-operating-decisions.md decision active team Engineering Operations Automation decision_linear-ontology-adoption decision_ideas-and-promote-workflow decision_deflate-ontology doc:workspace/charlie/notes/note_2026-09-14-knowledge-graph-v2-design.md doc:workspace/charlie/notes/note_2026-09-14-procedural-graphs-paper-ingest.md code:https://github.com/hey-mgmt-io/hey-mgmt-intelligence doc:content/playbooks/playbook_auditor-scope-d-deploy.md ## Context

The Knowledge Graph v2 design left six decisions open. Decision 1 (where the projection lives) was taken on 2026-09-14: the sibling repo `hey-mgmt-intelligence`. On the same day charlie confirmed decision 2 and delegated 3 through 7 to the agent with the instruction "you decide". This ADR records all of them so Phase 1 can start.

Facts that constrain the choices, from the first build of the projection over this repo:

- 4,679 of 9,436 authored edges (49.6%) are the untyped `links_to` produced by the bare-string `relations:` shorthand.
- 56 relations use off-vocabulary types that the validator only warns about; the projection migrates them on every build.
- `content/vocab/members.yml` already carries `fisher` (`role: agent-runtime`) and a generic `agent` entry, so an agent identity registry exists.
- The `hey-mgmt-io` org has 38 repos; the registry listed 20 before 2026-09-14.
- The pilot procedure graph has 6 nodes; the paper's graphs have 7 to 17.

## Decisions

### D1. Procedure representation: `x_procedure_graph` in playbook frontmatter

Procedural graphs live in the playbook's frontmatter under `x_procedure_graph` (schema `procedural-graph/v0`). No eighth artifact type, by the confusability test of `decision_deflate-ontology`. A sidecar file is permitted only when a graph exceeds 30 nodes, and the playbook MUST then point at it with `x_procedure_graph_file`. Rationale: one file, one owner, one `updated_at`, validated by the same tooling as every other artifact; the paper's evidence favours small graphs, so the ceiling is rarely reached.

### D2. Gate policy: metric where one exists, owner review otherwise

Every edit to an accepted procedure graph enters as `status: proposed`. The gate that turns it into `accepted` depends on the procedure class:

| Procedure class | Gate | Score |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ceremonies (`/morning`, `/snap`, `/night`, `/sync`, iteration turn) | metric | ceremony completes with `./hey validate` clean; solver steps and tokens not worse than the retained graph over the next 5 runs |
| Auditor and ops-runtime operations (deploy, apply-scope, backfill, hedge lanes) | metric | the operation's own verification (`run_evaluation` verdict, evidence dir `verification-summary.json`, CI green) plus steps and tokens |
| Everything else | owner review | the playbook `owner` accepts or rejects; the reason is written into the proposal |

Ties are accepted, as in the paper's Equation 5. A metric-gated candidate that fails structural validation never reaches rollout. Rejected proposals are kept with `status: rejected` and a `reason`, and every later refinement of the same playbook receives them as negative evidence.

*Addendum 2026-09-14 (charlie).* The gate is a mgmt command, `./hey procedure gate`, because it is the one operation that writes to a playbook. The projection repo `hey-mgmt-intelligence` is read-only against mgmt: it validates (`kg propose`), localizes, and queries, and mgmt imports its validator and edit interface from the sibling checkout so there is one implementation. The one-shot relation/type migration commands were removed from `kg` after they were applied.

### D3. Agent identity: `members.yml` is the only identity registry

Humans are `member:<name>` and agents are `agent:<name>`; both names MUST resolve to an entry in `content/vocab/members.yml`. Agents carry `role: agent-runtime` (Fisher already does). No separate `agents.yml`. Only a `member:` identity may set an edge to `accepted`; an `agent:` identity may only create `proposed` edges or, for imports it produced, `heuristic_signal` edges. The projection rejects an `accepted` edge asserted by an agent at build time and reports it.

*Addendum 2026-09-14 (charlie, while implementing the auditor import).* A third identity class, `system:<name>`, names a deterministic pipeline that has its own promotion gate — today only `system:auditor`, whose facts pass `protocol_knowledge_strict_promotion_gate` before they are exported. Edges asserted by a `system:` identity keep their native strength and status. Facts the auditor holds from `fisher_agent_formalizer` are exported as `agent:fisher` with `heuristic_signal`, because their own caveats say they are source-asserted context, not verifier-confirmed truth.

### D4. `links_to` deprecation: warning for artifacts updated from 2026-09-15, error later

The bare-string shorthand and explicit `links_to` stay valid for the 4,679 existing edges. From 2026-09-15, `./hey validate` warns when an artifact whose `updated_at` is on or after that date carries a bare-string relation, naming the typed alternatives. The projection's `untyped_share` metric is tracked in `kg stats`; when it falls below 30% the warning becomes an error and a one-shot migration types the remainder. Rationale: an immediate error would block every commit on 4,679 edits nobody has time for; a warning scoped to touched artifacts moves the number without a flag day.

### D5. Auditor export: charlie owns it, tracked as a task

charlie owns the auditor's `graph-exchange/v0` export (`export_protocol_knowledge_jsonl` next to the existing `export_*_jsonl` tools), because auditor and observatory work defaults to charlie. Tracked as `task_export-protocol-knowledge-graph-exchange`. Until it lands, the `auditor:` namespace in the projection is empty and the two what-is graphs remain disjoint; the design's Phase 1 exit criterion is not met before this task is done.

### D6. Registry upkeep: creator adds the row the same day; `/clean` diffs weekly

Whoever creates a repo in `hey-mgmt-io` (or adds a repo we work in elsewhere) adds its row to `content/vocab/repos.yml` in the same working day, with `org`, `status`, and a one-line description. `/clean` runs `gh repo list hey-mgmt-io` and reports any org repo missing from the registry and any registry row whose repo is archived or gone. Rationale: the registry drifted to 20 of 38 without a check; a weekly diff costs one command.

### D7. Namespace `oa:` for the onchain-analysis research corpus (added 2026-09-14)

`hey-mgmt-io/onchain-analysis` (511 markdown documents: insights, strategy analyses, risk assessments, knowledge base, whale tracking) joins the projection as the `oa:` namespace. One node per document (`oa:doc:<path>`, kind by top-level directory, freshness anchored on `last_verified` or the last commit date), one node per row of `strategies/catalog.md` (`oa:strategy:S-NNN`). Edges are `mentions` from frontmatter `related:`, relative markdown links, S-NNN ids in paths, and `protocol:` matches onto auditor `market_venue` nodes, all asserted by `agent:onchain-analysis` as `heuristic_signal`. The auditor already cites 477 of these documents as evidence for 3,455 promoted facts; those citations become `evidenced_by` edges, which is the join between research and protocol facts. The corpus stays where it is; `kg` reads it from the sibling checkout and never writes to it.

## Options Considered

- **Eighth artifact type `procedure`.** Rejected: same concept as a playbook in another representation; fails the confusability test.
- **Metric gate for everything.** Rejected: most playbooks have no measurable outcome yet; forcing one would produce fake metrics.
- **Separate `agents.yml`.** Rejected: `members.yml` already resolves Fisher; two registries invite drift.
- **`links_to` as an immediate error.** Rejected: 4,679 edits with no owner; the metric-triggered flip gets the same result without a flag day.
- **Registry check in CI.** Deferred: `gh` auth in CI is not set up for this repo; `/clean` runs weekly with a human present.

## Consequences

- Phase 1 of the design can start. Its exit criterion (isolated nodes under 10%, one query joining auditor facts to mgmt artifacts) depends on D5.
- `scripts/lib/validate.mjs` gains one dated warning (D4). `.claude/commands/clean.md` gains one checklist item (D6).
- The projection (`hey-mgmt-intelligence`) enforces D3 at build time and reports violations.
- The design note's Section 9 is closed; new decisions get their own ADR.

## Follow-Ups

1. `task_export-protocol-knowledge-graph-exchange` (D5).
2. Implement D3 enforcement in the projection's build (reject agent-asserted `accepted` edges).
3. Add the `untyped_share` threshold check that flips D4 from warning to error.
4. First metric-gated proposal round on `playbook_auditor-scope-d-deploy` after five live uses.

documents.title: ADR: Consolidate Knowledge Graph projection into hey-mgmt with sanitized export
documents.text:
decision_adr-consolidate-intelligence-graph-into-mgmt ADR: Consolidate Knowledge Graph projection into hey-mgmt with sanitized export content/decisions/decision_adr-consolidate-intelligence-graph-into-mgmt.md decision active team Engineering Operations Automation decision_adr-kg-v2-operating-decisions doc:workspace/charlie/notes/note_2026-09-14-knowledge-graph-v2-design.md doc:content/decisions/decision_adr-kg-v2-operating-decisions.md # ADR: Consolidate Knowledge Graph Projection into hey-mgmt with Sanitized Export

## Context

On 2026-09-14, Decision 1 of `decision_adr-kg-v2-operating-decisions` placed the unified knowledge graph projection in a sibling repository, `hey-mgmt-intelligence`. While intended to protect `hey-mgmt`'s core portable boundary, running the projection in a separate repository introduced significant friction:

1. **Repo-switching overhead:** Humans and agents operating inside `hey-mgmt` had to navigate to `../hey-mgmt-intelligence` to execute `kg` CLI queries, run builds, or validate proposals, then return to `mgmt` to gate them.
2. **Interface fragmentation:** `hey` CLI in `mgmt` and `kg` CLI in `intelligence` were disjoint; `./hey search` and `./hey context compile` could not query the unified projection.
3. **Export requirement:** External consumers, downstream LLM agents, and partner dashboards need an exported knowledge graph. Since `mgmt` is already the primary repository for organizational intelligence (tasks, decisions, playbooks, procedures), hosting the export pipeline directly where knowledge is authored is far cleaner and more maintainable than bridging across multiple repositories.

## Decisions

### 1. Absorb `hey-mgmt-intelligence` into `hey-mgmt`

All projection logic, adapters, query utilities, and procedure guidance engines are integrated directly into `hey-mgmt` under `scripts/lib/intelligence/`.

- Built-in CLI: `./hey graph <build|stats|search|node|neighborhood|backlinks|children|path|isolated|guidance|import-auditor|export>`.
- Standalone compatibility: `scripts/kg.mjs` remains executable for backward-compatible calls (`node scripts/kg.mjs ...`).
- Local projection storage: `.kg/graph.sqlite` and `.kg/graph.jsonl` are generated locally within `hey-mgmt` (gitignored, disposable, rebuildable).

### 2. Sanitized Export (`hey graph export`)

Knowledge graph export is introduced as a first-class feature with strict sanitization boundaries:

- `--scope public` (default):
  - **Excludes:** Personal member workspaces (`workspace/*`), internal meeting notes (`mgmt:meeting`), raw external messages (`ext:slack-*`, `ext:drive-*`), and nodes carrying confidential/internal-only tags (`[Confidential]`, `[InternalOnly]`).
  - **Includes:** Public protocol knowledge (`auditor:*`), onchain analysis research (`oa:*`), playbooks and procedural graphs (`mgmt:playbook`, `proc:*`), and public decisions/notes in `content/`.
  - **Referential Integrity:** All edges touching excluded nodes are automatically purged to prevent dangling edges in the exported dataset.
- `--scope all`: Exports the full internal graph without filtering.
- `--format <jsonl|json|sqlite>`: Emits JSON Lines, formatted JSON, or a standalone self-contained SQLite database.

### 3. Retire Remote `hey-mgmt-io/hey-mgmt-intelligence`

With 100% of capabilities, adapters, and tests ported into `hey-mgmt` and verified, the remote GitHub repository `hey-mgmt-io/hey-mgmt-intelligence` is deleted, and its entry in `content/vocab/repos.yml` is marked `status: retired`.

documents.title: Meeting note distillation
documents.text:
playbook_meeting-note-distillation Meeting note distillation content/playbooks/playbook_meeting-note-distillation.md playbook Team active team Operations Documentation Automation playbook_style-guide playbook_style-guide-ko note_external-activity-integration-plan doc:content/notes/note_external-activity-integration-plan.md doc:content/tasks/2026/04/task_fix-google-drive-collector-cov.md ## Purpose

Use this playbook when turning meeting transcripts, Gemini notes, Google Docs, pasted meeting text, or imported external meeting notes into `meeting` artifacts.

The goal is faithful distillation. Meeting notes preserve the meeting's important structure, thesis, decisions, and action items. They do not flatten high-signal source sections into generic discussion bullets.

## Core Rule

If the source contains an authored `Summary`, `요약`, `Action Items`, or structured headings such as `###`, the agent MUST preserve that structure unless it is clearly duplicate or malformed.

Do not re-summarize a source summary into a shorter agent summary when the source summary already carries the main thesis. Clean wording and normalize style, but keep the source's information architecture.

## Raw Context Preservation

Canonical meeting notes MUST preserve the maximum useful work context, not only the final summary.

- Save the full transcript or connector-extracted meeting body under `content/meetings/YYYY/MM/assets/<meeting-id>/` whenever the source can be stored safely.
- Prefer `transcript.txt` for a verbatim transcript and `source-gemini.txt` or `source-notion.txt` for machine-generated notes. Record the asset in `sources` and add a SHA-256 hash when practical.
- If the source contains personal, HR, medical, privileged, credential, personal-finance, or purely social material, create a near-verbatim sanitized source instead of dropping the entire body. Replace only the sensitive span with an explicit marker such as `[REDACTED: medical]` or `[REDACTED: privileged legal]`.
- Preserve work-related disagreement, alternatives, failed approaches, assumptions, numbers, qualifiers, speaker-attributed claims, decision status, and unresolved questions. Repetition and filler MAY be removed; context that changes interpretation MUST remain.
- The readable meeting artifact SHOULD contain a detailed discussion flow in addition to conclusions, decisions, open questions, and action items. The source asset remains the evidence layer when the readable artifact is condensed.
- A source URL by itself is not raw-context preservation. If connector access supplied the body during import, persist the approved and sanitized work context in the repo.
- Never convert a participant proposal into an approved decision. Attribute claims and retain uncertainty exactly where the source does.

## Required Flow

1. Read the full source text before writing the artifact.
2. Extract the source outline:
   - top-level sections,
   - `Summary` or `요약`,
   - action items,
   - decisions,
   - open questions,
   - named examples, metaphors, and product theses.
3. Create the `meeting` artifact with `./hey new --type meeting`.
4. Preserve source-summary sections in a dedicated section such as `## Source Summary`, `## Core Thesis`, or the original heading translated into repo style.
5. Add a concise `## Summary` only after preserving the source structure.
6. Add `## Topics Discussed`, `## Decisions`, `## Open Questions`, and `## Action Items` as needed.
7. Run a heading coverage check before finalizing.
8. Run `./hey validate`.

## Coverage Check

Before declaring the meeting note complete, compare source headings against the artifact.

- Every high-signal source heading MUST appear as an artifact heading or be explicitly represented by a same-meaning heading.
- Every source action item MUST appear in `## Action Items`, unless it is a duplicate.
- Every source decision-grade claim MUST appear in `## Decisions`, `## Core Thesis`, or `## Summary`.
- Named examples, analogies, and thesis phrases MUST NOT be dropped. Examples: "Goldman Sachs 2008", "source Summary", "원재료 + 효모".
- If a source section is intentionally omitted, add a short note in the artifact explaining why.

## Anti-Patterns

- Do not collapse a structured source summary into one-line `Topics Discussed` bullets.
- Do not treat `Summary` or `요약` as raw material when it is the author's main synthesis.
- Do not replace concrete thesis language with generic labels such as "business potential" unless the concrete claims remain nearby.
- Do not invent owners for action items. Use `team` when the source does not assign an owner.
- Do not copy rough transcript wording when a clean paraphrase preserves meaning better.

## Time Handling

If the meeting date is known but the exact time is unknown:

- set `start_at` and `end_at` to a validation-safe placeholder on that date;
- add `x_time_unknown: true`;
- state the uncertainty only if it affects interpretation.

## Sources

Use a stable source reference when available, such as a Drive URL, Slack thread, or canonical artifact id. If the source is a local paste without a stable repo path, use a descriptive `sources.ref` such as `user-provided pasted transcript, YYYY-MM-DD`.

## Action Item Assignment
<!-- candidate:candidate_meeting_action_assignment_20261022_playbook_meeting-note-distillation -->
Effective for meetings registered or re-synced from 2026-10-22, under [Alice's standing instruction](../../workspace/alice/inbox/meeting-action-assignment-policy-2026-10-22.json). This extends the Required Flow: meeting registration is incomplete until the action-to-task coverage check below passes.

1. Agents MUST extract each genuine agreed action, its stated owner, deliverable, and any stated due date from the reviewed source. Suggestions, possible next steps, and external counterpart promises MUST retain that status; source text does not authorize executing the work. Private-source approval and protected-information rules still apply before canonical promotion.
2. Agents MUST resolve owners against `content/vocab/members.yml`, using speaker/name context to resolve aliases and transcription errors. Every actionable item with an unambiguous mapped owner MUST become a task assigned to that person, or link to an existing task for the same deliverable. Search existing tasks before creating one; a re-import or repeated follow-up MUST NOT create another task.
3. Use repo-approved CLI paths such as `./hey new --type task --owner <member>` or inbox promotion. New tasks MUST record the meeting and source in `sources`, link to the meeting through `relations`, and define a concrete completion test. The meeting MUST link back through `relations` and show the task wiki-link beside the action. Split independent deliverables when they have different accountable owners or exceed three acceptance criteria; do not invent a lead for a jointly owned item.
4. Preserve stated deadlines and commitments. An agreed, assigned action starts `ready`; a proposal remains `plan` if tracked, with its uncertainty explicit. A verified dependency can make work `blocked`. Registration alone MUST NOT mark work `doing` or `done`, reset an existing task's lifecycle, assign an invented deadline/iteration, or silently choose a priority. Bound execution to a weekly iteration when scheduling is agreed; larger work MUST be split.
5. If ownership is absent, ambiguous, unmapped, or shared without clear accountability, record `담당 확인 필요` in the meeting and send the unresolved assignment to the importing member's inbox for clarification. The existing `team` fallback is a holding label, not a completed personal assignment. Do not default to Alice or create an internal member for an external participant. Track an internal liaison's follow-up only when that person's responsibility is explicit.
6. Agents MUST notify every newly assigned owner through `./hey inbox send --to <member> --task <task-id>`, including the originating member when this automated import is their first assignment notice. Include the deliverable, stated due date or unknown date, and meeting link. For reassignment, notify the new owner; for unchanged existing tasks, reuse recorded notification evidence and do not repeat notices on every sync. These task notices are separate from the mandatory all-team `./hey meeting notify <meeting-id>` read notice.
7. Before reporting registration complete, account for every in-scope source action with a task ID, an existing-task match, or an explicit disposition such as proposal-only, owner clarification, or protected/out-of-scope exclusion. Record the source action key, owner, task ID, source version, and notification result in the intake/meeting record. Reuse stable action identity across edits; substantive changes update the existing deliverable rather than duplicating it. Failed task creation, linkage, or notification remains incomplete with a recorded retry, never silently complete.

Apply this policy to future registrations and source updates. Historical backfill requires its own requested scope. User approval of a private meeting also authorizes registering its clearly owned agreed actions under this policy; it does not authorize external messages, fund movements, deployment, or other execution.
