documents.text:
playbook_file-placement File Placement: How Artifacts Find Their Home content/playbooks/playbook_file-placement.md playbook active team Operations Documentation playbook_operating-philosophy playbook_golden-principles playbook_governing-artifact-maintenance decision_no-separate-kb-dir decision_ideas-and-promote-workflow doc:AGENTS.md doc:ARCHITECTURE.md doc:docs/OPERATING_GUIDE.md doc:content/decisions/decision_no-separate-kb-dir.md doc:content/decisions/decision_ideas-and-promote-workflow.md # File Placement: How Artifacts Find Their Home

## Purpose

Give humans and agents one canonical routing policy for where new information belongs. This playbook is the placement map. Dynamic search and repo exploration happen after the policy answers the class of artifact.

## Rule

Agents MUST consult this routing policy first, then explore the repo dynamically for nearby precedent, related artifacts, and existing IDs before writing anything.

Policy decides the class. Exploration decides the exact file and relations.

If a change updates this routing policy in practice, this playbook MUST be updated in the same work. See `playbook_governing-artifact-maintenance`.

## Routing Table

| What you have | Put it here | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared actionable work | `content/tasks/YYYY/MM/` | Tasks are the shared execution ledger |
| Shared decision and rationale | `content/decisions/` | Decisions capture commitments and trade-offs |
| Shared spec, finding, report, analysis, or idea | `content/notes/` | Notes are the catch-all knowledge artifact |
| Reusable procedure, runbook, convention, or team know-how | `content/playbooks/` | Playbooks hold repeatable operating knowledge |
| External protocol or vendor reference material | `docs/references/` | Reference docs are not team-authored canonical artifacts |
| Docs about how `hey-mgmt` itself works | `docs/` | Repo-operating documentation for this system |
| Personal draft, scratch work, or individual progress | `workspace/{name}/` | Personal work area before promotion |
| Raw intake not yet classified | `workspace/{name}/inbox/` | Inbox-first chaos containment |
| Personal continuity log | `workspace/{name}/logs/` | Daily continuity layer, not indexed artifacts |
| Derived output or runtime state | `index/`, `.hey/`, `.runtime/` | Derived or local-only, never canonical |

## Decision Procedure

1. Ask whether the information is personal or shared.
2. If it is personal, put it in `workspace/{name}/` unless it is raw intake or a daily log.
3. If it is shared, ask whether it is work, rationale, knowledge, or reusable instruction.
4. Route to `task`, `decision`, `note`, or `playbook` accordingly.
5. Only after choosing the class, search the repo for related artifacts, existing IDs, and vocabulary.

## Agent Procedure

Agents SHOULD follow this order:

1. Read this playbook for placement policy.
2. Use `./hey search` or `./hey context compile` to find nearby artifacts and prior work.
3. Inspect the local directory only as needed to resolve edge cases.
4. Link to existing artifacts with `relations` instead of copying content.

This avoids two failure modes:

- Pure exploration with no policy, which produces inconsistent placement.
- Giant hand-maintained indexes, which become stale and duplicate the repo structure.

## Space Mirror

Every member and agent MUST follow Codex Space Mirror after creating, updating, renaming, archiving, or removing eligible shared content. Publish one document per Page, maintain linked indexes, and preserve mgmt as canonical. If publication is unavailable, record pending paths, responsible member, and reason in a tracked workspace receipt. Source completion and mirror completion MUST be reported separately.

Reports is a cross-topic reading view. Reports stored as notes keep their canonical note type and location; Reports links to their existing document Pages. Personal workspaces and raw assets are excluded unless explicitly included. These rules do not install unattended synchronization.

## Placement Hooks

Use these hooks for placement-related changes:

### Input Hook

Before implementing a change, ask whether it changes where something belongs, what artifact type should be used, or how agents should route information.

If yes, this playbook is part of the intended write set.

### Output Hook

Before declaring the work complete, ask whether the actual routing rule changed.

If yes, this playbook MUST describe the new rule in the same change.

## Promotion Rule

If something starts as a personal draft but becomes team-relevant, promote it into `content/` rather than expanding the workspace into a parallel knowledge base.

Use these promotion targets:

| Draft matures into | Promote to |
| --- | --- |
| Shared backlog item | `content/tasks/` |
| Shared report or finding | `content/notes/` |
| Reusable instruction or convention | `content/playbooks/` |
| Team commitment or architecture choice | `content/decisions/` |

## Anti-Patterns

- Do not create a new top-level knowledge directory.
- Do not store shared evergreen knowledge only in a member workspace.
- Do not put cross-repo team conventions in root docs when they belong in `content/playbooks/`.
- Do not use `docs/` as a second canonical artifact graph.
- Do not hand-edit derived state under `index/`, `.hey/`, or `.runtime/`.

## Heuristics

- If the team needs to coordinate on it, review it, or cite it later, it belongs in `content/`.
- If the value is in repeated reuse, it is probably a `playbook`.
- If the value is in explaining what is true, it is probably a `note`.
- If the value is in deciding what we will do, it is probably a `decision`.
- If the value is in getting work done next, it is probably a `task`.

## Scalability

This model scales because the placement map stays short and stable while discovery stays dynamic:

- The map is hand-maintained policy.
- The repo index is derived discovery.
- Search and context compilation are on-demand lookup tools.

Keep the policy small. Let the index do the exhaustive work.

documents.title: ADR: Product initiative kickoff contract — dates, PRD, component tasks and scope baseline
documents.text:
decision_adr-product-initiative-kickoff ADR: Product initiative kickoff contract — dates, PRD, component tasks and scope baseline content/decisions/decision_adr-product-initiative-kickoff.md decision Team active team Product Operations Automation decision_adr-initiative-timeline-dates decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline playbook_product-initiative-kickoff doc:content/meetings/2026/10/meeting_hey-mgmt-weekly-2026-10-28.md file:content/meetings/2026/10/assets/meeting_hey-mgmt-weekly-2026-10-28/source-sanitized.txt doc:content/decisions/decision_weekly-engineering-review-and.md doc:content/decisions/decision_adr-initiative-timeline-dates.md doc:content/decisions/decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline.md user_request:claude-code session 2026-11-03 ## Context

The Oct 28 weekly traced Enfri slippage to late feedback, weak design
agreement and progress nobody could see. The accepted
`decision_weekly-engineering-review-and`
moved the weekly review onto initiatives, but set no minimum for what an
initiative must carry.

As of 2026-11-03, 16 of 73 initiative files carry `x_timeline_start`, none
link a PRD in a dedicated field, and no field separates product work from
business, marketing or operations work. Tasks under one initiative are not
grouped by the component they build, and nothing records which tasks were
planned at kickoff. A product initiative can therefore grow or shrink while
its progress percentage still looks healthy.

Business, marketing and operations work behave differently: completion
often depends on a partner, so a target date cannot always be set. This ADR
covers product initiatives only.

## Decision

### D1. Classify every initiative by kind

Initiatives carry `x_initiative_kind: product | business | marketing | ops`.
The rules below apply only to `product`. Rules for the other kinds are left
to a follow-up ADR.

### D2. A product initiative cannot be `active` without its kickoff contract

Before or at kickoff, a product initiative MUST carry:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `x_timeline_start` | Initiative start date (required, not optional as in the timeline ADR) |
| `x_timeline_end` | Initiative target date |
| `x_prd_doc` | Link to the shared PRD: goal, why this approach, scope, components, task plan |
| `x_components` | Component or feature list taken from the PRD |
| `x_kickoff_date` | Date the plan was frozen; baseline for scope changes |
| `x_baseline_tasks` | Task ids planned at kickoff |

The PRD MUST be shared with the team and linked before kickoff, not written
afterwards. A new product initiative starts in `plan`;
`./hey initiative kickoff <id>` checks the fields above, records
`x_kickoff_date` and `x_baseline_tasks`, and moves it to `active`. Procedure:
[`playbook_product-initiative-kickoff`](../playbooks/playbook_product-initiative-kickoff.md).

### D3. Product tasks are component-level deliverables with dates

Each task under a product initiative MUST carry:

- `child_of` the initiative,
- `x_component`: one value from the initiative's `x_components`,
- `x_start_date` and `x_target_date`.

A task is a reviewable deliverable of one component. Sub-steps go into that
task's `definition_of_done`, not into separate tasks.

`x_target_date` is the planned finish, not an external deadline. `due_date`
keeps the meaning set by
[`decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline`](decision_adr-three-layer-task-timeline.md):
it is set only when a partner or launch commitment exists. A missed
`x_target_date` is a weekly slip flag, not a daily overdue item.

### D4. Initiative definition of done = baseline tasks done

A product initiative is done when every task in `x_baseline_tasks`, plus any
task added through a recorded scope change, is `done` or explicitly
`archived` with a reason.

### D5. Scope changes are shown, not absorbed

The weekly report lists, per product initiative, tasks added after
`x_kickoff_date` and baseline tasks removed, archived or unlinked since. The
list is computed as a diff against `x_baseline_tasks`. Scope may change; it
may not change silently.

### D6. Missing items alert the owner through inbox and Slack, and red-flag the weekly

A gap is any of: missing D2 field, product task without `x_component`,
`x_start_date` or `x_target_date`, a `x_component` value not in the
initiative's list, or a passed `x_target_date` on an open task.

- **Inbox + Slack:** a weekday run sends one inbox item per initiative to
  its owner, delivered through Fisher's existing Slack inbox job. Reminders
  dedupe by initiative or task, missing field and recipient: the same missing
  item is reminded at most once a week, and an item lists only the gaps not
  already reminded that week.
- **Weekly report:** every gap renders as a red flag on the initiative card
  with the field to fill.
- **Validator:** new product initiatives created on or after 2026-11-03 fail
  `./hey validate` when D2 fields are missing. Existing ones get a warning
  until the owner backfills them.

## Consequences

- Progress becomes measurable against a fixed plan per component, and scope
  growth is visible in the weekly.
- Kickoff costs more: a PRD and dated task plan are needed before work
  starts. This is the intended cost.
- Owners face new inbox items during backfill. The once-a-week cap on
  repeat alerts limits noise in an inbox that already holds dozens of items.
- Dates in `x_target_date` are estimates; the weekly shows slips, and a slip
  is information, not failure.
- Implemented 2026-11-03: schema and validator rules, indexer fields,
  `./hey initiative check | kickoff | alert`, a hygiene section, `/task` and
  scaffold prompts, the `/weekly-report` red-flag and scope rendering, and the
  board timeline. Alerts reach Slack through Fisher's existing member-inbox
  job once the `hey-mgmt-product-initiative-alert` cron is registered on the
  Mac Mini (`task_register-fisher-product-initia`).
- Existing initiatives are not classified automatically: a missing kind is
  missing information. An agent-drafted proposal for the 51 active
  initiatives (27 product, 13 business, 3 marketing, 8 ops, 9 uncertain) is in
  `workspace/alice/note_initiative-kind-classification-proposal.md` for Alice
  and owners to confirm. Until a kind is set, the validator warns and the
  weekly flags the initiative as unclassified.
- A kickoff baseline is agreed with the owner, not reconstructed by an agent.
  For an existing initiative the owner reviews `./hey initiative kickoff --dry-run`
  and unlinks or archives tasks outside the agreed plan before running it.
- Rules for business, marketing and ops initiatives remain open
  (`task_decide-tracking-rules-for-busi`).

## Alternatives Considered

- **Weekly-report-only red flags.** Rejected: a flag seen once a week arrives
  after a week of untracked work; the owner needs the alert when the gap
  appears.
- **Reuse `due_date` for task finish dates.** Rejected: it would overturn the
  three-layer ADR and refill daily triage with schedule estimates.
- **Infer scope change from `created_at` only.** Rejected: it catches added
  tasks but misses removed or unlinked ones; an explicit baseline list does
  both.
- **One rule for all initiative kinds.** Rejected: partner-dependent
  business work cannot honestly commit to end dates.

documents.text:
playbook_codex-agent-compliance-guide Codex Agent Compliance Guide content/playbooks/playbook_codex-agent-compliance-guide.md playbook active team Operations Documentation Review playbook_golden-principles playbook_operating-philosophy playbook_governing-artifact-maintenance playbook_style-guide doc:AGENTS.md doc:content/playbooks/playbook_style-guide.md doc:content/playbooks/playbook_golden-principles.md doc:content/playbooks/playbook_operating-philosophy.md doc:content/playbooks/playbook_governing-artifact-maintenance.md doc:ARCHITECTURE.md # Codex Agent Compliance Guide

## Purpose

Make Codex follow the same operating contract as Claude-style agents in this repo. This guide is a short execution checklist for Codex sessions, not a replacement for `AGENTS.md`.

Codex MUST treat `AGENTS.md` as the primary rule source. When this guide and `AGENTS.md` differ, `AGENTS.md` wins.

## Start Checklist

Before changing files, Codex MUST:

1. Read `AGENTS.md` for repo rules.
2. Read the English or Korean style guide that matches the output language.
3. Run `./hey deps check "<intent>"` for change-intent work.
4. Run `./hey search "<topic>"` before creating a new artifact.
5. Use `./hey new --type <type> --title "..."` for new artifacts unless there is a clear reason to hand-write one.
6. Check `content/vocab/` before using owners, tags, projects, or entities.

Change-intent work includes update, change, deploy, migrate, rename, remove, integrate, and refactor requests.

## Retrieval Requests

Codex MUST follow `content/playbooks/playbook_retrieval-protocol.md` for
retrieval-intent requests. A request is retrieval-intent when the answer depends
on finding existing artifacts, prior discussion, git history, external activity
knowledge, attachments, or current repo state.

Codex MUST include compressed Retrieval Proof in the answer. Do not present one
definitive artifact or source unless the RP5 candidate and disconfirmation
requirements are satisfied or explicitly waived by the exact-file exception.

## Write Rules

Codex MUST:

- Edit only `content/` and `workspace/` for canonical repo knowledge.
- Avoid hand-editing `index/`, `.hey/`, or `.runtime/`.
- Keep frontmatter minimal and valid.
- Put nonstandard frontmatter fields under `x_*`.
- Use existing tags, entities, owners, and projects.
- Link with `relations` instead of copying content from another artifact.
- Back decision-grade claims with `sources`.
- Keep one artifact focused on one concern.

Codex SHOULD route reusable instructions to `content/playbooks/`, rationale to `content/decisions/`, work items to `content/tasks/`, and findings or specs to `content/notes/`.

## Git Rules

Codex MUST protect user work during git operations.

- Check `git status --short --branch` before pull, merge, rebase, or commit.
- If the worktree is dirty before pull, stash or otherwise preserve local edits first.
- If conflicts occur, preserve both local and incoming content unless the user explicitly chooses one side.
- Do not use destructive commands such as `git reset --hard` or `git checkout -- <path>` unless the user explicitly asks.
- After resolving conflicts in artifacts, run the principles review and `./hey validate`.
- When deliverables are deployed or work in a branch/worktree completes, merge the shipped changes back into `develop` or `main` (per repo convention; respecting release-ownership rules), sync the local primary checkout with `origin/main` or `origin/develop` (`0 ahead / 0 behind`), and remove all completed worktrees and merged branches (`git worktree remove`, `git worktree prune`, `git branch -d`).

## Completion Checklist

Before saying work is complete, Codex MUST:

1. Run a principles self-review against:
   - `content/playbooks/playbook_golden-principles.md`
   - `content/playbooks/playbook_operating-philosophy.md`
   - `ARCHITECTURE.md`
2. Fix any principle violation before final response.
3. Run `./hey validate`.
4. Surface dependency-check obligations in the response, even when the result is "none."
5. Report validation errors and material warnings.
6. Verify post-deployment closeout: deployed changes are merged back to `develop` or `main`, the local primary checkout is synced with `origin/main` or `origin/develop`, and all completed worktrees and merged branches are cleaned up (`git worktree list` and `git status -sb`).

For large validation output, summarize the result and name representative warnings instead of pasting the full log.

## Prompt Snippet

Use this at the top of Codex sessions when strict compliance matters:

```text
Follow content/playbooks/playbook_codex-agent-compliance-guide.md exactly.
Before change-intent work, run ./hey deps check "<intent>" and surface obligations.
Before creating artifacts, run ./hey search "<topic>".
For retrieval-intent requests, follow content/playbooks/playbook_retrieval-protocol.md and show compressed Retrieval Proof.
After artifact changes, run principles review and ./hey validate.
Preserve user work during git operations.
```

## Common Failures

- Skipping `./hey deps check` before change-intent work.
- Creating an artifact without checking for an existing one.
- Answering a retrieval request from one plausible hit without RP5
  disconfirmation.
- Using a tag, owner, project, or entity outside `content/vocab/`.
- Treating `./hey validate` warnings as hidden noise.
- Resolving git conflicts by choosing one side when the user asked to preserve both.
- Editing derived files instead of the canonical markdown contract.

playbook_product-initiative-kickoff Product Initiative Kickoff content/playbooks/playbook_product-initiative-kickoff.md playbook Team active team Product Operations decision_adr-product-initiative-kickoff doc:content/decisions/decision_adr-product-initiative-kickoff.md code:scripts/lib/product-initiative.mjs # Product Initiative Kickoff

## Purpose

Start every product initiative with a shared PRD, a dated plan of
component-level tasks, and a frozen baseline, so the weekly review can show
progress against the plan and any change of scope. Rules:
[`decision_adr-product-initiative-kickoff`](../decisions/decision_adr-product-initiative-kickoff.md).

## Scope

Applies to initiatives with `x_initiative_kind: product`. Business, marketing
and ops initiatives do not use this playbook yet.

## Steps

### 1. Create the initiative in `plan`

```bash
./hey new --type initiative --title "<title>" --owner <member> \
  --field "x_initiative_kind=product"
```

A product initiative starts in `plan`. It becomes `active` only through step 5.

### 2. Write and share the PRD

The PRD is shared with the team before kickoff. It states:

- **Goal:** the outcome and how it will be measured.
- **Why:** the problem, and why this approach over the alternatives.
- **Scope:** what is in and out.
- **Components:** the features or components the work splits into.
- **Task plan:** one deliverable per component, with owner, start and target
  dates.

Link it on the initiative: `x_prd_doc: <url>`. Copy the component names into
`x_components`.

### 3. Set the initiative dates

`x_timeline_start` and `x_timeline_end` (YYYY-MM-DD). `x_timeline_end` is the
target; it is not a `due_date`.

### 4. Create the component tasks

One task per reviewable deliverable of a component. Sub-steps go into that
task's `definition_of_done`, not into separate tasks. Each task carries:

```yaml
relations:
  - type: child_of
    target: initiative_<id>
x_component: <one of x_components>
x_start_date: YYYY-MM-DD
x_target_date: YYYY-MM-DD
```

`/task` asks for these when the parent is a product initiative. Use `due_date`
only for an external commitment.

### 5. Kick off

```bash
./hey initiative kickoff initiative_<id>
```

The command refuses when the dates, PRD link or component list are missing.
It records `x_kickoff_date`, freezes the current tasks into
`x_baseline_tasks`, and moves the initiative from `plan` to `active`.

### 6. Run it

- `./hey initiative check` shows gaps, slips, scope changes and progress per
  component.
- Fisher runs `./hey initiative alert` on weekday mornings. Each owner gets one
  inbox item per initiative with gaps, delivered to Slack. The same missing
  item is reminded at most once a week; an item lists only gaps not reminded
  that week.
- The weekly report shows a red flag for every gap and a scope line for every
  task added or removed after kickoff.

## Changing scope after kickoff

Adding or archiving a task is allowed. It shows in the weekly as a scope change
against the baseline; say why in the weekly. Do not re-run kickoff to hide a
change. The initiative is done when every baseline task, plus every task added
through a shown scope change, is `done` or `archived` with a reason.

## Backfilling an existing product initiative

Initiatives that were active before 2026-11-03 get a validator warning, not an
error. The owner, not an agent, sets `x_initiative_kind` and supplies the PRD,
dates and components. Then do steps 2 to 4, review
`./hey initiative kickoff initiative_<id> --dry-run`, unlink or archive any
linked task that is not part of the agreed plan, and run step 5. Agents MUST
NOT invent dates, components or a retrospective baseline.
